# Renderer messages

The messages between a host and a renderer's sandboxed frame, as the renderer SDK's
protocol module (exported by `@githubnext/projections/renderer`) defines and validates them. The
[renderer frame protocol](../contracts/renderer-frames.md) explains the exchange; most renderers use the
SDK's client instead of these messages directly.

## Protocol (`@githubnext/projections/renderer`)

### `AcceptedExtraction`

```ts
type AcceptedExtraction<A extends Array<RendererAccepts>> = { [I in keyof A]: A[I] extends { schema: infer S extends "graph/v0" | "dag/v0" | "treemap/v0" | "metrics/v0" | "api/v0" | "database/v0" | "architecture/v0"; vocabulary: infer V extends "dependency-injection/v0" | "infrastructure/v0" | "runtime-policy/v0" | "agentic-workflows/v0" | "scenarios/v0"; } ? ExtractionOf<S, V> : A[I] extends { schema: infer S extends "graph/v0" | "dag/v0" | "treemap/v0" | "metrics/v0" | "api/v0" | "database/v0" | "architecture/v0"; } ? ExtractionOf<S, never> : never; }[number]
```

The typed extraction a renderer that accepts `A` receives: the union of what each entry guarantees.

### `acceptsExtraction`

```ts
acceptsExtraction(accepts: Array<RendererAccepts> | undefined, extraction: { "schema": string; "vocabularies"?: Array<string> | undefined }): false | true
```

Whether a renderer that accepts `accepts` presents `extraction`. Every renderer without `accepts` does.

### `AnchorRect`

```ts
interface AnchorRect
```

A rectangle in the renderer document's viewport, in CSS px.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | `"height": number` | Height, never negative. |
| `width` | `"width": number` | Width, never negative. |
| `x` | `"x": number` | Left edge, relative to the viewport's left; within ±`rendererLimits.maxCoordinate`. |
| `y` | `"y": number` | Top edge, relative to the viewport's top; within ±`rendererLimits.maxCoordinate`. |

### `AnnotationMark`

```ts
interface AnnotationMark
```

A marker the host asks a renderer to draw on an item, for example a count
of comments or findings. `id` is the item's selection ID.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `count` | `"count"?: number` | A number to show, for example how many comments. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | The annotated item's selection ID, never empty. |
| `label` | `"label"?: string` | Short accessible description, for example `2 comments`. |
| `tone` | `"tone"?: "attention" \| "done" \| "neutral" \| "subtle"` | `attention` for something unresolved, `done` for something resolved. |

### `AnnotationTone`

```ts
type AnnotationTone = "attention" | "done" | "neutral" | "subtle"
```

One of `annotationTones`: how a marker reads, independent of the item's change status.

### `annotationTones`

```ts
annotationTones: readonly ["neutral", "attention", "done", "subtle"]
```

Marker tones, deliberately unlike change colors: `neutral`, `attention`
(something to act on, in the accent color), `done` (resolved, muted) and
`subtle` (for example outdated, with a dashed outline).

### `badgeDiscValue`

```ts
badgeDiscValue: string
```

A badge's disc by default (`--projections-icon-badge`): a solid circle filling the icon's box, as in icons.css.

### `badgeIconNames`

```ts
badgeIconNames: Array<"added" | "additive" | "agent" | "application" | "blocked" | "breaking" | "bytecode" | "changed" | "collapse" | "comparator" | "compatible" | "credential" | "downgraded" | "enforced" | "error" | "exclude" | "expand" | "extractor" | "file" | "generated" | "hidden" | "host" | "import" | "include" | "info" | "modified" | "module" | "moved" | "namespace" | "network" | "other" | "policy" | "process" | "read" | "redeploy" | "removed" | "renamed" | "renderer" | "replace" | "rescoped" | "settings" | "unenforced" | "unknown" | "upgraded" | "varied" | "visible" | "warning" | "workload">
```

The icons drawn as badges, a solid disc with the glyph cut out of it, so they read as marks rather than text: the
change kinds (`added` to `moved`, and a version's `upgraded`, `downgraded` or `changed`), the planned actions
(`replace` to `blocked`) and `breaking`, which sits beside them in a change's status. Every other icon is an
outline glyph: severity, compatibility levels, the policy and coverage notes a comparator adds after a change's
status, and `varied`. A note asks for an outline icon of its own, never a change kind's.

### `ColorMode`

```ts
type ColorMode = "dark" | "light"
```

Whether the host is in light or dark mode; renderers draw in the same mode.

### `ColorTokenName`

```ts
type ColorTokenName = "accent" | "accent-emphasis" | "accent-muted" | "added" | "added-border" | "added-emphasis" | "added-highlight" | "added-muted" | "bg" | "bg-inset" | "bg-overlay" | "bg-subtle" | "border" | "border-emphasis" | "border-muted" | "divider" | "fg" | "fg-muted" | "fg-on-emphasis" | "fg-subtle" | "focus" | "highlight" | "modified" | "modified-border" | "modified-emphasis" | "modified-highlight" | "modified-muted" | "moved" | "moved-border" | "moved-emphasis" | "moved-highlight" | "moved-muted" | "removed" | "removed-border" | "removed-emphasis" | "removed-highlight" | "removed-muted" | "surface-canvas" | "surface-header" | "surface-inset" | "surface-raised"
```

Color token names without `color-`, such as `fg-muted` or `added-border`.

### `ComparisonMode`

```ts
type ComparisonMode = "animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe"
```

One of `comparisonModes`.

### `comparisonModes`

```ts
comparisonModes: readonly ["diff", "side-by-side", "animated", "swipe"]
```

How a host presents a comparison with a renderer:

- `animated`: one frame, driven through `progress` from before to after.
- `side-by-side`: two frames, one held at progress 0 and one at 1.
- `swipe`: the same two frames stacked, with a divider between them.
- `diff`: one frame and no `progress` at all; the renderer draws its own
  static comparison of both subjects (`init.comparisonMode` is `'diff'`).

```ts
type ControlIcon = "collapse" | "download" | "expand" | "filter" | "fit" | "next" | "previous" | "reset" | "search" | "settings" | "zoom-in" | "zoom-out"
```

One of `controlIcons`, an action control's optional icon.

### `controlIcons`

```ts
controlIcons: readonly ["zoom-in", "zoom-out", "fit", "reset", "expand", "collapse", "previous", "next", "download", "filter", "search", "settings"]
```

Icons hosts map to their design system for action controls.

```ts
type ControlValue = false | number | string | true
```

A control's value: a choice's `value`, a toggle's boolean or a range's number.

### `defaultComparisonMode`

```ts
defaultComparisonMode(modes: Array<"animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe">): "animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe"
```

The mode a comparison opens in: the renderer's first supported mode in
canonical order, so diff when it supports diff, else side by side. A
renderer chooses only which modes it supports.

### `defaultComparisonModes`

```ts
defaultComparisonModes: Array<"animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe">
```

The modes a renderer supports when it declares none: every progress-driven mode.

### `describeAccepts`

```ts
describeAccepts(accepts: Array<RendererAccepts>): string
```

`accepts` in words: `` `database/v0` `` or `` `architecture/v0` with `dependency-injection/v0` ``.

### `Envelope`

```ts
interface Envelope
```

The fields every protocol message carries. A message whose version or channel doesn't match is not part of this
conversation, and both sides ignore it.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `channel` | `"channel": string` | The frame's channel nonce from the URL fragment: 16 to 128 letters, digits, `_` or `-`. |
| `projections` | `"projections": 0` | The protocol version, `rendererProtocolVersion`. |

### `FilterPayload`

```ts
interface FilterPayload
```

The host's find and "changes only" settings, as `filter` carries them. Renderers that declare `filter` de-emphasize
or hide the items `ids` leaves out; `query` and `changesOnly` are for describing the state, not for matching again.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `changesOnly` | `"changesOnly": false \| true` | Whether the person asked to see only changed items; `ids` already reflects it. |
| `ids` | `"ids": Array<string> \| null` | Matching selection IDs, or `null` when every item is shown or more than `rendererLimits.filterIds` match. |
| `query` | `"query": string` | The find query as typed, or an empty string. |

### `FontSizeStep`

```ts
type FontSizeStep = "lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs"
```

Steps of the type scale: `xs` (12px) to `xl` (20px); `md` is the body size, the `font-size` token.

### `FontWeightStep`

```ts
type FontWeightStep = "bold" | "medium" | "normal" | "semibold"
```

Font weights: `normal` (400), `medium` (500), `semibold` (600) and `bold` (700).

### `HostEnvelope`

```ts
type HostEnvelope = Envelope & { "height": number; "type": "viewport"; "width": number } | Envelope & { "id": null | string; "path"?: string; "type": "select" } | Envelope & { "id": null | string; "type": "hover" } | Envelope & { "id": string; "type": "action" } | Envelope & { "items": Array<AnnotationMark>; "type": "annotations" } | Envelope & { "options": RendererOptions; "type": "options" } | Envelope & { "type": "document" } & { "renderer": string } & { "error": string; "html"?: never } | Envelope & { "type": "document" } & { "renderer": string } & { "error"?: never; "html": string } | Envelope & { "type": "environment" } & RendererEnvironment | Envelope & { "type": "filter" } & FilterPayload | Envelope & { "type": "init" } & RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } | Envelope & { "type": "init" } & RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" } | Envelope & { "type": "progress" } & ProgressPayload | Envelope & { "type": "scroll" } & ScrollPosition
```

A host message as posted to the frame: the message with the protocol version and channel.

### `HostMessage`

```ts
type HostMessage = { "height": number; "type": "viewport"; "width": number } | { "id": null | string; "path"?: string; "type": "select" } | { "id": null | string; "type": "hover" } | { "id": string; "type": "action" } | { "items": Array<AnnotationMark>; "type": "annotations" } | { "options": RendererOptions; "type": "options" } | { "type": "document" } & { "renderer": string } & { "error": string; "html"?: never } | { "type": "document" } & { "renderer": string } & { "error"?: never; "html": string } | { "type": "environment" } & RendererEnvironment | { "type": "filter" } & FilterPayload | { "type": "init" } & RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } | { "type": "init" } & RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" } | { "type": "progress" } & ProgressPayload | { "type": "scroll" } & ScrollPosition
```

Every message a host sends a renderer, without its envelope (`HostEnvelope`), as `parseHostMessage` accepts it.
`connectRenderer` hands each to the matching `RendererHandlers` member; a renderer receives `init` first and again
whenever the document changes, and every other message may arrive at any time after it.

### `iconMaskStyle`

```ts
iconMaskStyle(name: string): { [key: string]: string }
```

The mask that draws icon `name` where the SDK's icons.css doesn't apply, such as a host's own UI, exactly as
icons.css draws it in a frame: its token (`--projections-icon-<name>`, defined on the element or an ancestor) and,
for a badge (`badgeIconNames`), the disc (`--projections-icon-badge`, a circle by default) with the glyph cut out.
Camel-cased CSS properties for a style object; give the element a size and a `currentColor` background. A name the
theme lacks draws nothing.

### `IconName`

```ts
type IconName = "added" | "additive" | "agent" | "application" | "blocked" | "breaking" | "bytecode" | "changed" | "collapse" | "comparator" | "compatible" | "credential" | "downgraded" | "enforced" | "error" | "exclude" | "expand" | "extractor" | "file" | "generated" | "hidden" | "host" | "import" | "include" | "info" | "modified" | "module" | "moved" | "namespace" | "network" | "other" | "policy" | "process" | "read" | "redeploy" | "removed" | "renamed" | "renderer" | "replace" | "rescoped" | "settings" | "unenforced" | "unknown" | "upgraded" | "varied" | "visible" | "warning" | "workload"
```

A name in the icon vocabulary (`iconNames`); validate untrusted input with `isIconName`.

### `iconNames`

```ts
iconNames: readonly ["added", "removed", "modified", "renamed", "moved", "warning", "error", "breaking", "info", "unknown", "additive", "compatible", "upgraded", "downgraded", "changed", "enforced", "unenforced", "include", "exclude", "visible", "hidden", "expand", "collapse", "rescoped", "settings", "agent", "replace", "redeploy", "import", "read", "blocked", "varied", "generated", "host", "policy", "workload", "credential", "process", "file", "network", "module", "bytecode", "namespace", "application", "other", "extractor", "comparator", "renderer"]
```

The icon vocabulary: semantic names a renderer asks for, never a specific
glyph. Each is a theme token, `icon-<name>`, whose value is a CSS image
(an SVG data URL) that renderers draw as a mask in `currentColor`, so its
shape comes from the host and its color from the text beside it. An icon
never carries meaning alone: it always accompanies its word.

- Changes: `added`, `removed`, `modified`, `renamed`, `moved`.
- Severity: `warning`, `error`, `breaking`, `info`, `unknown`.
- Compatibility and versions: `additive`, `compatible`, `upgraded`,
  `downgraded`, `changed` (changed either way).
- Policy and coverage: `enforced`, `unenforced`, `include`, `exclude`,
  `visible`, `hidden`, `expand`, `collapse`, `rescoped` (a scope changed
  either way), `settings`, `agent`.
- Planned actions: `replace`, `redeploy`, `import`, `read`, `blocked`.
- Volatile data: `varied`, a volatile value (one an extraction declares may
  vary between runs) that changed beyond its tolerance. Neutral, never a
  change kind: draw it in the text color beside the change's own status.
  `generated`, a value an extractor generated from a recorded basis (a
  summary a language model wrote, say): the quiet mark beside every
  generated field's name. Neutral, never a change kind.
- Subjects, what a section holds, beside its title: `host` (the nodes a
  system runs on), `policy`, `workload`, `credential`, `process`, `file`,
  `network`, `module` (a loadable extension, such as a kernel module),
  `bytecode` (a loaded program, such as BPF), `namespace` (an isolation
  boundary or mount), `application` (user-space programs) and `other`.
- Projection parts: `extractor`, `comparator`, `renderer`. Their own
  drawings, not Lucide's: a dot is the extraction, the same size in all
  three; strokes converge on it (extract), two dots sit either side of a
  dashed divider (compare), and strokes leave it (render).

### `iconTokenLength`

```ts
iconTokenLength: 4096
```

The longest icon token value a host may send (an SVG data URL), in UTF-16 code units.

### `IconTokenName`

```ts
type IconTokenName = "icon-added" | "icon-additive" | "icon-agent" | "icon-application" | "icon-blocked" | "icon-breaking" | "icon-bytecode" | "icon-changed" | "icon-collapse" | "icon-comparator" | "icon-compatible" | "icon-credential" | "icon-downgraded" | "icon-enforced" | "icon-error" | "icon-exclude" | "icon-expand" | "icon-extractor" | "icon-file" | "icon-generated" | "icon-hidden" | "icon-host" | "icon-import" | "icon-include" | "icon-info" | "icon-modified" | "icon-module" | "icon-moved" | "icon-namespace" | "icon-network" | "icon-other" | "icon-policy" | "icon-process" | "icon-read" | "icon-redeploy" | "icon-removed" | "icon-renamed" | "icon-renderer" | "icon-replace" | "icon-rescoped" | "icon-settings" | "icon-unenforced" | "icon-unknown" | "icon-upgraded" | "icon-varied" | "icon-visible" | "icon-warning" | "icon-workload"
```

The theme token that holds an icon's image, `icon-<name>` (`iconToken`).

### `InitPayload`

```ts
type InitPayload<X extends Extraction = Extraction> = RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": X; "before": X; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } | RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": X; "mode": "extraction" }
```

What the host sends a renderer to present. `X` is the extraction type: a renderer that declares what it
accepts (`RendererManifest.accepts`) can narrow it, with `AcceptedExtraction`, to the typed extractions
the engine guarantees. Every entity and relationship carries `data`, `{}` when the extraction omits it.

### `isControlValue`


an entity kind, and has no `shape`.

| `shape` | `"shape"?: "circle" \| "dashed" \| "dotted" \| "line" \| "square"` | Default `square`. |

"shadow-sm" \| "space-1" \| "space-2" \| "space-3" \| "space-4" \| "space-5" \| "space-6" \| "space-7" \| "space-8"` | The swatch as a theme token, which follows the host's theme. |

### `LegendShape`

```ts
type LegendShape = "circle" | "dashed" | "dotted" | "line" | "square"
```

One of `legendShapes`: a filled `square` or `circle`, or a solid, `dashed` or `dotted` stroke for relationships.

### `legendShapes`

```ts
legendShapes: readonly ["square", "circle", "line", "dashed", "dotted"]
```

How a legend item's swatch is drawn: a `square` or `circle` of color, or a
short `line`, `dashed` line or `dotted` line. `dotted` came later: a host
that can't draw it draws it `dashed`.

### `optionalThemeTokenNames`

```ts
optionalThemeTokenNames: readonly ["stage-inset", "stage-inset-top", "stage-max-height", "color-connector"]
```

Layout tokens a host may send that have no default (`resolveThemeTokens` leaves them undefined), so a renderer reads
each with its own value as the fallback: `stage-inset`, the space between the frame's edges and its content on every
side, `stage-inset-top`, the space above the content where the host overlays the frame's top, and `stage-max-height`,
the most a content-sized stage that pans and zooms asks for (`px`, or `vh` of the host's window), and
`color-connector`, the color of lines that carry meaning (a graph's links), for a host whose `color-divider` is its
app's own quiet rule rather than a 3:1 edge; renderers fall back to `color-divider`.

### `orderComparisonModes`

```ts
orderComparisonModes(modes: Array<"animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe">): Array<"animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe">
```

Modes in the order hosts show them, whatever order a renderer declares
them in: diff, side by side, animated, then swipe (`comparisonModes`).

### `parseAccepts`

```ts
parseAccepts(value: unknown): Array<RendererAccepts> | undefined
```

Distinct, known `accepts` entries, or undefined.

### `parseComparisonModes`

```ts
parseComparisonModes(value: unknown): Array<"animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe"> | undefined
```

Validates a `comparisonModes` declaration: a non-empty list of distinct known modes, in any order.

### `parseControls`

```ts
parseControls(value: unknown): Array<{ "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": false | true; "type": "toggle" } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "icon"?: "collapse" | "download" | "expand" | "filter" | "fit" | "next" | "previous" | "reset" | "search" | "settings" | "zoom-in" | "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }> | undefined
```

Validates control declarations strictly: unique IDs, at most
`rendererLimits.controls` controls and `rendererLimits.choices` choices each,
known types and icons, defaults that are valid values.

### `parseHostMessage`

```ts
parseHostMessage(value: unknown, channel: string): undefined | { "height": number; "type": "viewport"; "width": number } | { "id": null | string; "path"?: string; "type": "select" } | { "id": null | string; "type": "hover" } | { "id": string; "type": "action" } | { "items": Array<AnnotationMark>; "type": "annotations" } | { "options": RendererOptions; "type": "options" } | { "type": "document" } & { "renderer": string } & { "error": string; "html"?: never } | { "type": "document" } & { "renderer": string } & { "error"?: never; "html": string } | { "type": "environment" } & RendererEnvironment | { "type": "filter" } & FilterPayload | { "type": "init" } & RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } | { "type": "init" } & RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" } | { "type": "progress" } & ProgressPayload | { "type": "scroll" } & ScrollPosition
```

Validates the shape of a host-to-renderer message. Documents inside `init`
are produced and validated by the host's engine; this checks the envelope
and message structure only.

### `parsePace`

```ts
parsePace(value: unknown): RendererPace | undefined
```

Validates a `pace` declaration: exactly `{stepMs}`, an integer within `rendererLimits.paceStepMs`.

### `parseRendererManifest`

```ts
parseRendererManifest(value: unknown): RendererManifest
```

Validates a parsed `renderer.json` strictly and returns a normalized copy without unknown or absent fields.

### `parseRendererMessage`

```ts
parseRendererMessage(value: unknown, channel: string): undefined | { "capabilities": RendererCapabilities; "type": "ready" } | { "controls": Array<{ "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": false | true; "type": "toggle" } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "icon"?: "collapse" | "download" | "expand" | "filter" | "fit" | "next" | "previous" | "reset" | "search" | "settings" | "zoom-in" | "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }>; "type": "controls" } | { "ends": Array<number>; "slots"?: number; "type": "steps" } | { "id": null | string; "path"?: string; "type": "select" } | { "id": null | string; "type": "hover" } | { "id": string; "rect": AnchorRect | null; "type": "anchor" } | { "id": string; "type": "annotation" } | { "line"?: number; "path": string; "type": "open" } | { "message": string; "type": "error" } | { "progress": number; "type": "rendered" } | { "px": number; "type": "height" } | { "ratio": number; "type": "aspect" } | { "renderer": string; "type": "document-request" } | { "type": "legend" } & RendererLegend | { "type": "summary" } & RendererSummary | { "type": "viewport" } & ScrollPosition
```

Validates a renderer-to-host message strictly. Returns `undefined` for
anything that is not exactly one of the protocol messages, including
unknown fields, out-of-range numbers and oversized text.

### `parseSummaryItems`

```ts
parseSummaryItems(value: unknown): Array<SummaryCountItem | SummaryFactItem> | undefined
```

Validates a summary's figures strictly (the `items` of a `summary` message): at most `rendererLimits.summaryItems`.
A count item (`type` `count` or absent) names a non-empty `kind` once per collection (`collection`, optional); a
fact item (`type` `fact`) has a distinct non-empty `id`, an optional `icon` name, an optional `tone`, at most
`rendererLimits.summaryFactIds` non-empty `ids`, optional `added`, `removed` and `modified` counts and an optional
`description` (non-empty, at most `rendererLimits.summaryDescription` characters). Both have a `noun` of exactly
`singular` and `plural` (non-empty, at most `rendererLimits.summaryNoun` characters) and non-negative integer
counts. An item of an unknown `type` is dropped and the rest kept, so later types stay additive; anything else
invalid refuses the whole summary.

### `ProgressPayload`

```ts
interface ProgressPayload
```

Presentation position. `progress` runs from 0 (before) to 1 (after);
`highlighting` is the change-emphasis strength the host chose for this
position (exactly 0 at both endpoints); `direction` is the playback direction.
Extraction mode always uses `{progress: 1, highlighting: 0, direction: 1}`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | `"direction": -1 \| 1` | `1` while playing or scrubbing forward, `-1` backward, for motion that differs by direction. |
| `highlighting` | `"highlighting": number` | How strongly to emphasize changes at this position, from 0 (none) to 1 (full); draw it, don't derive it. |
| `progress` | `"progress": number` | Position in the transition, from 0 (`before`) to 1 (`after`); the host validates only that it is finite. |

### `RadiusStep`

```ts
type RadiusStep = "full" | "lg" | "md" | "sm"
```

Steps of the corner radius scale: `sm` (6px) to `lg` (10px), and `full` for pills; `md` is the `radius` token.

### `readRendererFragment`

```ts
readRendererFragment(hash: string): undefined | { "channel": string; "colorMode"?: "dark" | "light"; "hostOrigin": string }
```

Reads the channel nonce, host origin and color mode from a renderer document's URL fragment.

### `RendererAccepts`

```ts
interface RendererAccepts
```

An extraction a renderer presents: one in domain schema `schema` and, with `vocabulary`, declaring that
vocabulary. Without `vocabulary`, any extraction in the schema matches, whatever vocabularies it declares.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `schema` | `"schema": "api/v0" \| "architecture/v0" \| "dag/v0" \| "database/v0" \| "graph/v0" \| "metrics/v0" \| "treemap/v0"` | The domain schema the extraction is in, for example `architecture/v0`. |
| `vocabulary` | `"vocabulary"?: "agentic-workflows/v0" \| "dependency-injection/v0" \| "infrastructure/v0" \| "runtime-policy/v0" \| "scenarios/v0"` | A vocabulary the extraction must declare, for example `dependency-injection/v0`. |

### `RendererCapabilities`

```ts
interface RendererCapabilities
```

What a renderer supports, declared once in `ready` (`ConnectOptions.capabilities`). Hosts send the optional messages
(`hover`, `scroll`, `filter`, `annotations`) only to renderers that declare them, and the renderer checks hold each
declared capability to its contract. Optional flags default to off, except `drawsRelationships`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `anchors` | `"anchors"?: false \| true` | Whether the renderer reports where the selected and hovered entities are (`anchor`). |
| `annotations` | `"annotations"?: false \| true` | Whether the renderer draws the host's `annotations` and reports `annotation` when one is activated. |
| `changeHighlighting` | `"changeHighlighting": "none" \| "supported"` | Whether the renderer visibly emphasizes changes using `highlighting`. |
| `comparisonModes` | `"comparisonModes"?: Array<"animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe">` | Comparison modes the renderer supports. Hosts show them in canonical order and open in the first: diff when it is supported, else side by side (`defaultComparisonMode`); the declared order doesn't matter. Without it, `defaultComparisonModes`. The same list belongs in the bundle's `renderer.json`, so a host can offer the right modes before the frame loads. |
| `controls` | `"controls"?: Array<{ "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } \| { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": false \| true; "type": "toggle" } \| { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } \| { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "icon"?: "collapse" \| "download" \| "expand" \| "filter" \| "fit" \| "next" \| "previous" \| "reset" \| "search" \| "settings" \| "zoom-in" \| "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }>` | Controls the host draws for the renderer, in display order. Values arrive in `options` under each control's `id`; actions arrive as `action`. A renderer may replace them later with a `controls` message. |
| `drawsRelationships` | `"drawsRelationships"?: false \| true` | Whether the renderer draws relationships as elements marked with the relationship's ID in `data-entity-id`. Defaults to true; declare `false` only when it deliberately draws none, or shows them only as structure (nesting, order), so the renderer checks don't expect them. |
| `filter` | `"filter"?: false \| true` | Whether the renderer honors the host's `filter`. |
| `hover` | `"hover"?: false \| true` | Whether the renderer reports and shows hover (`hover` in both directions). |
| `ownTimeline` | `"ownTimeline"?: false \| true` | Whether the renderer presents its own timeline; the host still owns progress. |
| `pace` | `"pace"?: RendererPace` | The pace the renderer's motion reads best at: `stepMs`, how long one comparison step should take during playback (an integer from `rendererLimits.paceStepMs.min` to `.max`). Hosts that size playback by the step count use it in place of their default; the person's own speed setting still applies on top, and the host still owns progress. |
| `properties` | `"properties"?: false \| true` | Whether the renderer draws item properties and may report them as `select` with a `path`. |
| `scrollSync` | `"scrollSync"?: false \| true` | Whether the renderer reports scrolling (`viewport`) and follows `scroll`. |
| `toggleableRelationships` | `"toggleableRelationships"?: false \| true` | Whether the renderer honors `options.showRelationships`. |

### `rendererContentSecurityPolicy`

```ts
rendererContentSecurityPolicy: string
```

Content security policy for renderer documents. Serving layers send it as
a response header with every renderer bundle's `index.html`. A bundle is a
single self-contained document: scripts and styles are inline and other
assets are data or blob URLs, so the policy grants no source at all, not
even `'self'`, and the document load is the only request a renderer causes.
The `sandbox` directive keeps the document in an opaque origin even if it
is opened outside the host frame.

### `RendererControl`

```ts
type RendererControl = { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": false | true; "type": "toggle" } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "icon"?: "collapse" | "download" | "expand" | "filter" | "fit" | "next" | "previous" | "reset" | "search" | "settings" | "zoom-in" | "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }
```

A setting the host draws for the renderer. By `type`:

- `choice`: one of `choices` (distinct non-empty `value`s of at most 64 characters, each labelled), `default` among
  them; its value is the chosen `value`.
- `toggle`: a boolean, `default` on or off.
- `range`: a number from `min` to `max` (`min < max`) in `step` increments (`step > 0`), `default` within them,
  with an optional short `unit` such as `%`.
- `action`: a button with an optional `icon`; it has no value, and activating it sends `action` with its `id`.

`parseControls` validates a list strictly and `controlValues` reads the values.

### `RendererDocument`

```ts
type RendererDocument = { "renderer": string } & { "error": string; "html"?: never } | { "renderer": string } & { "error"?: never; "html": string }
```

A built-in renderer's document as the host supplies it (`document`): the bundle's `index.html` text, exactly as the
host would load it into its own frame, or why the host can't supply it. Exactly one of `html` and `error`.

### `RendererEnvelope`

```ts
type RendererEnvelope = Envelope & { "capabilities": RendererCapabilities; "type": "ready" } | Envelope & { "controls": Array<{ "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": false | true; "type": "toggle" } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "icon"?: "collapse" | "download" | "expand" | "filter" | "fit" | "next" | "previous" | "reset" | "search" | "settings" | "zoom-in" | "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }>; "type": "controls" } | Envelope & { "ends": Array<number>; "slots"?: number; "type": "steps" } | Envelope & { "id": null | string; "path"?: string; "type": "select" } | Envelope & { "id": null | string; "type": "hover" } | Envelope & { "id": string; "rect": AnchorRect | null; "type": "anchor" } | Envelope & { "id": string; "type": "annotation" } | Envelope & { "line"?: number; "path": string; "type": "open" } | Envelope & { "message": string; "type": "error" } | Envelope & { "progress": number; "type": "rendered" } | Envelope & { "px": number; "type": "height" } | Envelope & { "ratio": number; "type": "aspect" } | Envelope & { "renderer": string; "type": "document-request" } | Envelope & { "type": "legend" } & RendererLegend | Envelope & { "type": "summary" } & RendererSummary | Envelope & { "type": "viewport" } & ScrollPosition
```

A renderer message as posted to the host: the message with the protocol version and channel.

### `RendererEnvironment`

```ts
interface RendererEnvironment
```

The host's presentation context: theme, motion preference, locale and frame role. `init` carries it and
`environment` replaces it; `applyEnvironment` exposes it to CSS.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `locale` | `"locale": string` | BCP 47 locale for formatting, for example `en-US`. |
| `pane` | `"pane"?: "after" \| "before"` | Set while the frame is one held pane of a two-pane comparison mode (side by side or swipe): it shows only the `before` (progress 0) or `after` (progress 1) revision, which the host labels. Narration of the transition, such as step captions, doesn't apply there; omit it. Absent for a single frame (animated, diff or an extraction). |
| `reducedMotion` | `"reducedMotion": false \| true` | Whether the person prefers reduced motion: skip the renderer's own animations (pulses, eased transitions) and draw each `progress` as it arrives. `applyEnvironment` marks it as `data-reduced-motion`. |
| `sizing` | `"sizing"?: "content" \| "fill"` | How the host sizes the frame. `content`: it gives the frame the height the renderer reports (`height`, within `rendererLimits`), so content fitted to the frame need only fit its width, from the first paint on, rather than the height the frame has before the host answers. `fill`: it sizes the frame itself, as a tab or pane does, and content fits both dimensions. Absent from hosts that don't say: fit both dimensions. |
| `theme` | `"theme": RendererTheme` | The host's theme tokens and color mode. |

### `RendererFocus`

```ts
interface RendererFocus
```

What a host wants a renderer's opening view to show, for example an image of a comparison's changes or of one item.
Content that doesn't fit its frame opens on it instead of at the renderer's reading start; the person can still zoom
and scroll. A renderer that fits everything anyway may ignore it. Without it, a renderer opens as it chooses: a
comparison in diff mode opens on its changes when they don't all fit.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fit` | `"fit"?: false \| true` | Fit what is focused into the view even when that draws its smallest text below the opening floor (`openingFloorPx`), which a renderer otherwise keeps to and scrolls the rest: for images that must show it whole. |
| `id` | `"id"?: string` | The selection ID of one item to open on, centred with what it connects to where they fit. |
| `on` | `"on"?: "all" \| "changes"` | `changes`: the comparison's changed items and the relationships between them (in a held pane, those its revision has); `all`: everything. Ignored when `id` names an item. |

### `rendererFragment`

```ts
rendererFragment(channel: string, hostOrigin: string, colorMode?: "dark" | "light" | undefined): string
```

The URL fragment the host appends to a renderer entry URL: the channel
nonce, the host origin and, optionally, the color mode, so the document can
match the host's colors before `init` arrives.

### `RendererKind`

```ts
interface RendererKind
```

How the definition presents one extraction kind (see `RendererProjection.kinds`).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `color` | `"color"?: "amber" \| "blue" \| "citron" \| "cyan" \| "danger" \| "emerald" \| "green" \| "indigo" \| "info" \| "lime" \| "neutral" \| "orange" \| "pink" \| "purple" \| "red" \| "rose" \| "sky" \| "success" \| "teal" \| "violet" \| "warning"` | The kind's color: a meaning or a categorical hue, which renderers paint with theme tokens. |
| `noun` | `"noun"?: { "plural": string; "singular": string }` | The kind's noun for counts, for example `{singular: 'service', plural: 'services'}`. |

### `RendererLegend`

```ts
interface RendererLegend
```

A renderer's legend: an optional title and its items; no items clears it.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | `"items": Array<LegendItem>` | The entries in display order, at most `rendererLimits.legendItems`. |
| `title` | `"title"?: string` | A heading for the legend, 1 to `rendererLimits.legendLabel` characters. |

### `rendererLimits`

```ts
rendererLimits: { "annotationCount": 1000000; "annotationLabel": 64; "annotations": 10000; "aspect": { "max": 100; "min": 0.01 }; "choices": 50; "controls": 32; "documentTimeoutMs": 10000; "filterIds": 20000; "legendItems": 24; "legendLabel": 64; "maxCoordinate": 1000000; "maxHeight": 20000; "messageBytes": number; "messagesPerSecond": 240; "minHeight": 120; "paceStepMs": { "max": 5000; "min": 300 }; "readyTimeoutMs": 10000; "steps": 1000; "summaryDescription": 256; "summaryFactIds": 1000; "summaryItems": 32; "summaryKind": 256; "summaryNoun": 64; "textLength": 4096; "themeTokens": 256; "tokenLength": 512 }
```

Bounds the host enforces on renderer-to-host messages.

### `RendererManifest`

```ts
interface RendererManifest
```

Manifest each renderer bundle ships as `renderer.json` beside its `index.html`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `accepts` | `"accepts"?: Array<RendererAccepts>` | The extractions the bundle presents; absent means any. See `RendererAccepts`. |
| `comparisonModes` | `"comparisonModes"?: Array<"animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe">` | Comparison modes the bundle supports (see `RendererCapabilities.comparisonModes`); absent means `defaultComparisonModes`. |
| `format` | `"format": "projections.renderer"` | Identifies the file as a renderer manifest. |
| `handles` | `"handles": Array<string>` | Definition renderer names this bundle presents, for example `["graph", "dag"]`. |
| `name` | `"name": string` | Bundle directory name, for example `basic`. |
| `title` | `"title": string` | The renderer's human-readable name, which hosts show in their messages and menus; 1 to 200 characters. |
| `version` | `"version": 0` | The manifest format version; hosts reject any other. |

### `RendererMessage`

```ts
type RendererMessage = { "capabilities": RendererCapabilities; "type": "ready" } | { "controls": Array<{ "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": false | true; "type": "toggle" } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } | { "description"?: string; "group"?: string; "groupLabel"?: string; "id": string; "label": string } & { "icon"?: "collapse" | "download" | "expand" | "filter" | "fit" | "next" | "previous" | "reset" | "search" | "settings" | "zoom-in" | "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }>; "type": "controls" } | { "ends": Array<number>; "slots"?: number; "type": "steps" } | { "id": null | string; "path"?: string; "type": "select" } | { "id": null | string; "type": "hover" } | { "id": string; "rect": AnchorRect | null; "type": "anchor" } | { "id": string; "type": "annotation" } | { "line"?: number; "path": string; "type": "open" } | { "message": string; "type": "error" } | { "progress": number; "type": "rendered" } | { "px": number; "type": "height" } | { "ratio": number; "type": "aspect" } | { "renderer": string; "type": "document-request" } | { "type": "legend" } & RendererLegend | { "type": "summary" } & RendererSummary | { "type": "viewport" } & ScrollPosition
```

Every message a renderer sends its host, without its envelope (`RendererEnvelope`), as `parseRendererMessage`
accepts it. Renderers post them through `RendererClient`, which clamps and validates them; the host drops any that
fail validation or exceed `rendererLimits`.

### `rendererMetaContentSecurityPolicy`

```ts
rendererMetaContentSecurityPolicy: string
```

The same policy for a `<meta http-equiv>` element, which cannot carry the
`sandbox` directive. Built bundles include it so static hosting without
header control still forbids network access; hosts must not rely on it for
untrusted bundles.

### `rendererNamePattern`

```ts
rendererNamePattern: RegExp
```

A renderer name, as `renderer.json` declares it.

### `RendererOptions`

```ts
interface RendererOptions
```

The renderer's settings as the host last sent them in `options`: each declared control's value under its `id`
(read them with `controlValues`, which falls back to defaults), plus any options the host sets itself. Each
`options` message replaces the whole object.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `[string]` | `[key: string]: unknown` |  |
| `showRelationships` | `"showRelationships"?: false \| true` | Whether to draw relationships, for renderers that declare `toggleableRelationships`; absent means draw them. |

### `RendererPace`

```ts
interface RendererPace
```

The playback pace a renderer reads best at (`RendererCapabilities.pace`).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `stepMs` | `"stepMs": number` | Milliseconds per comparison step: an integer within `rendererLimits.paceStepMs`, else `ready` is invalid. |

### `RendererProjection`

```ts
interface RendererProjection
```

The projection a renderer presents, as `init` names it.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `"id": string` | The projection definition's ID, stable across documents of the same projection. |
| `kinds` | `"kinds"?: { [key: string]: RendererKind }` | How the definition presents extraction kinds (`presentation.kinds`), keyed by kind: a color for renderers that color items by kind (a meaning or a categorical hue, painted with theme tokens) and the summary bar's noun. Hosts send it when the definition sets it; renderers ignore kinds they don't draw. |
| `renderer` | `"renderer": string` | The definition's renderer: its renderer name (for example `graph-horizontal`), or the bundle path of a custom renderer. A bundle that handles several names uses it to choose a variant. |
| `title` | `"title": string` | The definition's title, for headings and accessible names. |

### `rendererProtocolVersion`

```ts
rendererProtocolVersion: 0
```

Renderer frame protocol, version 0.

A renderer is a static web bundle that the host loads into
`<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">` (an opaque origin) served with a content
security policy that includes `connect-src 'none'`. The host and the
renderer exchange `postMessage` envelopes that carry the protocol tag and a
per-frame channel nonce, which the host passes in the frame URL fragment.

### `rendererSandbox`

```ts
rendererSandbox: "allow-scripts"
```

The only sandbox tokens a host grants a renderer frame. Never add `allow-same-origin`.

### `RendererSummary`

```ts
interface RendererSummary
```

A renderer's summary: its figures in display order; no items returns the bar to the host's own words.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | `"items": Array<SummaryCountItem \| SummaryFactItem>` | The figures, at most `rendererLimits.summaryItems`, in the order the bar shows them. |

### `RendererTheme`

```ts
interface RendererTheme
```

Host theme. Tokens are CSS values keyed by name without the leading
dashes, for example `{"color-fg": "#1f2328"}`; `applyEnvironment` exposes
them to renderer CSS as `--projections-<name>`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `colorMode` | `"colorMode": "dark" \| "light"` | The host's color mode, which `applyEnvironment` sets as the document's `color-scheme`. |
| `tokens` | `"tokens": { [key: string]: string }` | Token values by name, at most `rendererLimits.themeTokens`, each at most `rendererLimits.tokenLength` characters; `icon-*` tokens hold icon values (`isIconValue`). Read them through `resolveThemeTokens`, which fills in defaults. |
| `version` | `"version"?: number` | The token set the host follows (`themeTokenSetVersion`). Missing tokens fall back to that set's defaults. |

### `resolveThemeTokens`

```ts
resolveThemeTokens(theme: { "colorMode": "dark" | "light"; "tokens": { [key: string]: string } }): Record<string, string>
```

A host's tokens over the defaults, so every token of the current set is defined.

### `ScrollPosition`

```ts
interface ScrollPosition
```

A scroll position in CSS px. `key` identifies the scroll container so that
two panes of the same renderer can mirror each other: the value of its
`data-projections-scroll` attribute, or a structural path. Omitted for the
document itself.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `"key"?: string` | The scroll container: 1 to 256 letters, digits, spaces or `_.:>-`. Absent for the document. |
| `x` | `"x": number` | Horizontal scroll offset, never negative. |
| `y` | `"y": number` | Vertical scroll offset, never negative. |

### `SpaceStep`

```ts
type SpaceStep = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8
```

Steps of the space scale: `space-1` (4px) to `space-8` (48px).

### `SummaryCountItem`

```ts
interface SummaryCountItem
```

A count figure of the summary bar the host draws along every projection view: how many items of an extraction
`kind` (entity or relationship) there are, in the renderer's own word for them. `count` is the total in the
extraction, or in `after` for a comparison; `added`, `removed` and `modified` count the comparison's changes of that
status whose item has the kind (an added or modified change by its `after` item, a removed one by its `before` item),
and are omitted for one extraction. The previous total ("was N") is `count − added + removed`, so it is never sent.
`collection` tells an entity kind from a relationship kind of the same name. Hosts show their own counts of the
named kinds, so the counts are what the renderer checks verify; the vocabulary, and which kinds appear in what
order, are the renderer's. `type` is optional and defaults to `count`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `added` | `"added"?: number` | In a comparison, added items of the kind (by their `after` item). |
| `collection` | `"collection"?: "entities" \| "relationships"` | Which items `kind` names: entities or relationships. Absent, both (a kind that names either). |
| `count` | `"count": number` | Items of the kind in the extraction, or in `after` for a comparison; a non-negative integer. |
| `kind` | `"kind": string` | The extraction kind counted, 1 to `rendererLimits.summaryKind` characters; each kind once per collection. |
| `modified` | `"modified"?: number` | In a comparison, modified items of the kind (by their `after` item). |
| `noun` | `"noun": SummaryNoun` | The renderer's word for items of the kind. |
| `removed` | `"removed"?: number` | In a comparison, removed items of the kind (by their `before` item). |
| `type` | `"type"?: "count"` | Marks a count figure; the default when absent. |

### `SummaryFactItem`

```ts
interface SummaryFactItem
```

A fact figure of the summary bar: a finding of the renderer's domain that no kind count says, such as `2 breaking
changes` or `3 unprotected routes`. `id` is its stable key; `icon` names a theme icon token (`--projections-icon-<name>`,
none without it); `count` and `noun` are its words (singular for 1); `tone` colors the figure. With `ids`, the
entity or relationship IDs (or comparison change IDs) it is about, the figure filters to those items as a count
figure filters to its kind. In a comparison, `added`, `removed` and `modified` are its changes, which hosts draw
after it in the change colors as they draw a count figure's: how many of the things it counts arrived, left or
changed, or for a measure of each revision (`39,882 lines of code`) its net change, `added` when it grew and
`removed` when it shrank, so the previous value is `count − added + removed` as for a count. `description` is one
sentence of context hosts show as its tooltip and accessible description, such as the rules that decided it.
Hosts show a fact as the renderer sends it; the renderer checks verify its shape, that its `ids` exist and that a
single extraction's facts have no changes.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `added` | `"added"?: number` | In a comparison, how many of the counted things arrived, or a measure's net growth. |
| `count` | `"count": number` | The figure's number, a non-negative integer. |
| `description` | `"description"?: string` | One sentence of context, at most `rendererLimits.summaryDescription` characters, shown as the figure's tooltip. |
| `icon` | `"icon"?: string` | A theme icon token's name without its `icon-` prefix: a lowercase identifier; no icon when absent. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | Stable key, distinct among the summary's facts, 1 to `rendererLimits.summaryKind` characters. |
| `ids` | `"ids"?: Array<string>` | The items the fact is about, at most `rendererLimits.summaryFactIds`; activating the figure filters to them. |
| `modified` | `"modified"?: number` | In a comparison, how many of the counted things changed. |
| `noun` | `"noun": SummaryNoun` | The figure's words; `singular` for a `count` of 1, else `plural`. |
| `removed` | `"removed"?: number` | In a comparison, how many of the counted things left, or a measure's net shrinkage. |
| `tone` | `"tone"?: "added" \| "modified" \| "neutral" \| "removed"` | The figure's change color; absent or `neutral`, none. |
| `type` | `"type": "fact"` | Marks a fact figure. |

### `SummaryFactTone`

```ts
type SummaryFactTone = "added" | "modified" | "neutral" | "removed"
```

One of `summaryFactTones`: the change color of a fact's figure, or `neutral` for none.

### `summaryFactTones`

```ts
summaryFactTones: readonly ["added", "removed", "modified", "neutral"]
```

The tones a summary fact may take: a change hue on its figure, or none.

### `SummaryItem`

```ts
type SummaryItem = SummaryCountItem | SummaryFactItem
```

One figure of the summary bar: a count of an extraction kind (`type: 'count'`, the default) or a domain fact
(`type: 'fact'`). Hosts drop an item of a `type` they don't know, keeping the rest, so new types stay additive.

### `SummaryNoun`

```ts
interface SummaryNoun
```

A noun of the renderer's domain, for one item and for any other count: `{singular: 'workspace', plural: 'workspaces'}`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `plural` | `"plural": string` | The word for zero or several items, 1 to `rendererLimits.summaryNoun` characters. |
| `singular` | `"singular": string` | The word for exactly one item, 1 to `rendererLimits.summaryNoun` characters. |

### `supportedComparisonModes`

```ts
supportedComparisonModes(declared: undefined | { "comparisonModes"?: Array<"animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe"> | undefined }): Array<"animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe">
```

The comparison modes a renderer supports, in canonical order (see `defaultComparisonMode`).

```ts
svgIconValue(svg: string): string
```

An SVG document as a CSS image value, for an icon token.

### `themeTokenSetVersion`

```ts
themeTokenSetVersion: 0
```

### `token`

```ts
token: { "chart": { (index: number): string }; "color": { (name: "accent" | "accent-emphasis" | "accent-muted" | "added" | "added-border" | "added-emphasis" | "added-highlight" | "added-muted" | "bg" | "bg-inset" | "bg-overlay" | "bg-subtle" | "border" | "border-emphasis" | "border-muted" | "divider" | "fg" | "fg-muted" | "fg-on-emphasis" | "fg-subtle" | "focus" | "highlight" | "modified" | "modified-border" | "modified-emphasis" | "modified-highlight" | "modified-muted" | "moved" | "moved-border" | "moved-emphasis" | "moved-highlight" | "moved-muted" | "removed" | "removed-border" | "removed-emphasis" | "removed-highlight" | "removed-muted" | "surface-canvas" | "surface-header" | "surface-inset" | "surface-raised"): string }; "fontSize": { (step: "lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs"): string }; "fontWeight": { (step: "bold" | "medium" | "normal" | "semibold"): string }; "radius": { (step: "full" | "lg" | "md" | "sm"): string }; "space": { (step: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8): string }; "var": tokenVar }
```

Theme tokens as CSS values, typed so a name that isn't a token doesn't compile. Prefer the kit's components and
their props; use these for an inline style the kit doesn't cover, such as `style={{gap: token.space(2)}}`. The
renderer checks (`palette`, `type-scale`, `spacing`) hold every painted value to these.
